newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch builders merge to form Volker Wessels Stevin.
newsitem.headline: Dutch builders merge to form Volker Wessels Stevin.

text.p: Construction firm Volker Stevin NV on Tuesday unveiled plans to merge with sector rival Kondor Wessels Groep to create a new company, Volker Wessels Stevin NV.

"The planned merger will be based on equal terms... and achieved technically by an exchange of Kondor Wessels Groep shares for (depositary receipts of share in) Royal Volker Stevin," the two companies said in a joint statement.
Volker spokesman Gerrit Anneveldt said the deal, creating a company with annual turnover of some four billion guilders had effectively been sealed subject to shareholder approval.
"Both parties agree it is a good deal," he said.
"The intention is to publish the official merger notice at end-April 1997," the companies' statement said.
It said the proposed terms of share exchange were based on an analysis of the respective companies' financial results, share prices, and profit and cash flow projections.
These took into account the conversion of the remaining part of Volker Stevin's 5.25 percent convertible bond issue and options to be exercised at both companies.
The merger would create a company with a leading position in all domestic construction sectors, the partners said.
The combine would also occupy a favourable position in the general building and housing construction sectors in several German regions and in the industrial building and supplies sector.
"In addition the new company will have foreign market positions in Belgium, Britain and North America which complement its core activities," the companies said.

Key advantages of the merger were greater stability due to a more even spread of activities in general building and infrastructure, a good geographical spread on the domestic market, and a good position on the building supply market.
It would also create a good springboard for further growth in core activities in Germany and a bigger financial base, the joint statement said.
